extracted.intended_audience: graduate students / advanced undergraduates in analysis / measure theory; professional mathematicians studying Riesz representation and regular Borel measures
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing and verifying the regular Borel measure associated to a positive linear functional on Cc(X) for a locally compact Hausdorff space X, and proving its properties (additivity, regularity, extension, uniqueness) and related results (Baire sets, density, weak-* compactness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of µ on compact sets
rubrics_metrics.description: If K is compact, define µ(K) to be the infimum of `(f) over all f in Ccom(X) such that IK ≤ f (i.e., f is ≥ the indicator of K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic construction: µ(K) := inf{ `(f) : f ∈ Ccom(X), 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on K }. It is used as the starting point for extension to larger classes of sets and for proving regularity and uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension to ring (X) via differences of compacts
rubrics_metrics.description: µ extends in a well-defined fashion to a nonnegative additive set function on the ring (X) under the definition µ(⋃_{j=1}^n (K_j − L_j)) = ∑_{j=1}^n µ(K_j − L_j) whenever K_j and L_j are compact with L_j ⊆ K_j for each j and the sets K_j − L_j are pairwise disjoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lemma addresses the subtlety that the representing compact sets K_j need not be disjoint; it shows additivity is well-defined for finite disjoint unions of set differences of compacts. The proof reduces to checking consistency under different decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete additivity on (X)
rubrics_metrics.description: µ is completely additive on (X): for any disjoint sequence {E_n} in (X) with union E in (X), µ(E) = ∑_n µ(E_n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses regularity and covering compact cores by bounded open sets; choose compact K and bounded open U approximating E, use finite subcovers of K, and pass to limits to obtain countable additivity. This property is needed before applying the Extension Theorem to obtain a measure on the σ-ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension to σ-ring and Borel σ-algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: µ (initially defined on (X)) extends uniquely to a measure on the smallest σ-ring containing (X) (the σ-ring of σ-bounded Borel sets), and then canonically to a measure on the σ-algebra of all Borel sets by µ(E) = sup{ µ(F) : F ⊆ E, F σ-bounded }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Extension Theorem (Theorem 5.5) and Proposition 5.37. This extension preserves additivity and yields a (regular) Borel measure agreeing with the original µ on compact sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outer regularity (approximation by open sets)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any σ-bounded set E in the relevant σ-ring (or for bounded sets), µ(E) = inf{ µ(U) : U open bounded, U ⊇ E }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularity is shown by, given ε>0, finding compact K and bounded open U with K ⊆ E ⊆ U and µ(U) − µ(K) < ε. This outer approximation conclusion is used repeatedly to pass from compact approximants to general sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inner regularity (approximation by compact sets)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any σ-bounded set E (or bounded open U), µ(E) = sup{ µ(K) : K compact, K ⊆ E }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 11.13: for bounded open U, µ(U) = sup_{K ⊆ U, K compact} µ(K). More generally regularity gives the inner regularity statement for σ-bounded (and hence for compact) sets. Used to show `(f) = ∫ f dµ for f ∈ Cc(X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity property used in extension/definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The constructed µ on (X) satisfies: for each ε>0 there exist compact K and open bounded U with K ⊆ E ⊆ U and µ(U) − µ(K) < ε (the stated regularity property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit regularity condition is central to proving µ is a regular Borel measure after extension and to establish equalities of µ with integrals of approximating continuous functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of positive linear functionals by integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a positive linear functional ` on Ccom(X), the constructed regular Borel measure µ satisfies `(f) = ∫_X f dµ for every f ∈ Ccom(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core Riesz Representation conclusion: define µ on compacts by infima of `(f), extend to (X) and to Borel sets, then use dominated convergence / test functions to verify equality for all f ∈ Ccom(X). Uniqueness of µ follows from uniqueness on compact sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of the representing regular Borel measure
rubrics_metrics.description: If ∫ is a second regular Borel measure satisfying the same properties (i.e., `(f) = ∫ f d∫ for all f ∈ Ccom(X)), then ∫(K) = µ(K) for every compact K, hence ∫ = µ on Borel sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: if ∫(K) < µ(K) for some compact K one constructs a test function g with IK ≤ g ≤ IU for open U and gets contradiction via definitions of µ(K) as an infimum. Regularity of the second measure is used to find appropriate U.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baire sets and measurability of Ccom(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: The σ-algebra B0(X) generated by compact Gδ's (Baire sets) contains the supports of members of Ccom(X), and every member of Ccom(X) is a Baire function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition/Corollary chain: compact Gδ's and Fσ open sets are used to show Ccom(X) functions are Baire measurable. In metric spaces Baire and Borel σ-algebras coincide; otherwise Baire sets are helpful when using Fubini.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity of Baire measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Baire measure µ is regular in the Baire sense: for E ∈ B0(X), µ(E) = sup{ µ(K) : K compact Gδ, K ⊆ E } and for σ-bounded E, µ(E) = inf{ µ(U) : U open Fσ ⊇ E }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 11.18: the same inner/outer regularity holds with compact Gδ and open Fσ approximants. This is used to extend Baire measures uniquely to regular Borel measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and uniqueness of Baire measures to regular Borel measures
rubrics_metrics.description: If ∫ is a Baire measure, there is a unique regular Borel measure µ on X whose restriction to the Baire sets is ∫.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 11.19: construct the positive linear functional `(f) = ∫ f d∫ on Ccom(X), apply Riesz representation to get µ and then verify µ agrees with ∫ on compact Gδ's and hence on all Baire sets by regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity preserved under absolute continuity on compact X
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is compact and µ is a regular Borel measure and ∫ is a Borel measure absolutely continuous with respect to µ, then ∫ is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Radon–Nikodym to obtain density and control small µ-measure sets to show outer/inner approximations for ∫. (Proposition 11.20.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of Ccom(X) in L^p and approximation by indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: If µ is a regular Borel measure and 1 ≤ p < ∞, then (a) Ccom(X) is dense in L^p(X, µ), and (b) the smallest closed subspace of L^p(X, µ) containing all indicator functions of compact Gδ's is L^p(X, µ) itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 11.21: use regularity to approximate Borel sets of finite measure by compact Gδ's and bounded open sets, then use dominated convergence on approximating Ccom sequences for indicator functions and standard L^p density arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separability results in σ-compact metric spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a locally compact separable metric space and µ is a Borel measure, then (a) Ccom(X) (with sup norm) is separable, and (b) L^p(X, µ) is separable for 1 ≤ p < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 11.22: use σ-compactness and compact exhaustion Fn with separability of C(Fn) to produce countable dense subsets; combine with Proposition 11.21 to deduce separability of L^p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helly–Bray compactness (weak-* limit of measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a sequence {µ_n} of Borel measures on a locally compact separable metric space X with µ_n(X) bounded by M, there exists a subsequence µ_{n_k} and a Borel measure µ with µ(X) ≤ M such that ∫ f dµ_{n_k} → ∫ f dµ for all f ∈ Ccom(X) (weak-* convergence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 11.23: interpret measures as continuous linear functionals on the normed space Ccom(X); use Banach–Alaoglu (preliminary form) plus separability of Ccom(X) to extract subsequence converging pointwise on Ccom(X), then invoke Riesz to realize the limit as a measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to compact case and extension of linear functionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any continuous linear functional on Ccom(X) is uniformly continuous and extends uniquely to C0(X); further extensions to C(X*) (one-point compactification) exist but nonuniquely. Thus studying duals reduces to the compact case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use density of Ccom(X) in C0(X) and the fact that continuous linear functionals are uniformly continuous; then identify continuous functionals on C(X) (compact X) with regular Borel measures via Riesz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition of continuous linear functionals into positive parts
rubrics_metrics.description: For compact X and a continuous linear functional ` on C(X) (real-valued on real functions), define `+(f) = sup{ `(g) : 0 ≤ g ≤ f } and `− = `+ − `. Then `+ and `− extend to positive linear functionals and ` = `+ − `−; more generally any continuous linear functional is a complex combination of positive linear functionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 11.24: this is the functional-analytic analogue of Jordan decomposition for signed measures. The construction verifies positivity, homogeneity, subadditivity, and yields representation of functionals as differences (or complex linear combinations) of positive functionals, which correspond to (regular) measures.
